quickSummary: Frogs execute gas exchange through 3 routes: Cutaneous (passive diffusion across moist vascular skin; operates on land, in water, and 100% during hibernation/aestivation), Buccopharyngeal (buccal floor oscillations with glottis closed), and Pulmonary (positive-pressure buccal force-pump driven by sternohyal lowering and petrohyal raising of buccal floor with glottis open).

conceptBreakdown.content: Frogs perform gas exchange through three distinct anatomical pathways depending on environmental medium and metabolic demand.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Comparative Respiratory Mechanisms Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Comparative Respiratory Mechanisms Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Parameter | Cutaneous Respiration | Buccopharyngeal Respiration | Pulmonary Respiration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Organ / Surface** | Moist vascularized **Integument (Skin)** | Mucous membrane lining of **Buccopharyngeal Cavity** | Pair of pink, ovoid, sac-like **Lungs** |
| **Environmental Context** | Operates in water, on land, and **exclusively during Hibernation & Aestivation** | Operates on land while resting | Operates on land during elevated physical activity |
| **Mechanism** | Simple passive diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ across moist skin capillary beds | Pumping action created by raising and lowering the buccal cavity floor | Force-pump mechanism driven by buccal muscles (**Sternohyal** and **Petrohyal**) |
| **State of Glottis** | Not involved | **CLOSED** (Air moves through nares into buccal cavity without entering lungs) | **OPENED** (Air forced from buccal cavity through glottis into lungs) |
| **Vascular Network** | Cutaneous artery and cutaneous vein branches | Rich capillary plexus of buccal mucosa | Pulmocutaneous artery and pulmonary vein branches |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Mechanics of Pulmonary Respiration
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Mechanics of Pulmonary Respiration
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PULMONARY INSPIRATION MECHANICS
                       
  1. Buccal Floor Lowered ──► Sternohyal muscles contract ──► Pressure Drops
                             (External nares OPEN, Glottis CLOSED)
                             Fresh air drawn into Buccal Cavity.
                             
  2. Glottis Opens         ──► Pulmonary air (high CO₂) released/mixed.
  
  3. Buccal Floor Raised  ──► Petrohyal muscles contract ──► Pressure Rises
                             (External nares CLOSED, Glottis OPEN)
                             Air FORCED under positive pressure into Lungs.
conceptBreakdown.content:
Because frogs lack ribs and a diaphragm, pulmonary ventilation relies on a positive-pressure **Buccal Force-Pump Mechanism**:
$$\text{External Nares} \rightarrow \text{Nasal Cavities} \rightarrow \text{Internal Nares} \rightarrow \text{Buccopharyngeal Cavity} \rightarrow \text{Glottis} \rightarrow \text{Lungs}$$
